heard: Your calendar ran 11 minutes long. It cost 10 days. Not a war and not a plague, just one leap day, too many. A year is 365 days and almost six hours. Skip them and you're a day off every four years. So add a leap day every four years. That's 365 and a quarter, the old Julian calendar. But a quarter day is too much. The real year is 11 minutes shorter. 11 minutes a year is a day every 128 years. By 1582, spring arrived on 11 March, not 21 March. So Pope Gregory deleted 10 days. Thursday the 4th of October was followed by Friday the 15th. Then dropped three leap days every 400 years. 1 ,700, 1 ,800 and 1 ,900 skipped. 2 ,000 stays. Now your year runs long by 27 seconds. One day every 3 ,200 years. So is 2 ,100 a leap year.
